content:
REASON FOR REFERRALU: Diagnostic test by Whole Exome Sequencing (WES).
Patient has a clinical presentation of X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets (information supplied with referral) and has been tested as part of the diagnostic Whole Exome Sequencing service in our laboratory.

TEST
Test for sequence variants in a virtual panel of skeletal genes by WES analysis.
Any variant(s) detected by WES is confirmed by Sanger sequencing 

RESULTS
Hemizygous PHEX c.2063_2064dupAT p.(Ala689fs) variant detected

SUMMARYU 
The presence of the PHEX c.2063_2064dupAT p.(Ala689fs) variant is confirmed in patient. Variants in GENE have previously been reported to cause autosomal dominant hypophosphatemic rickets, X-linked. 

The PHEX c.2063_2064dupAT p.(Ala689fs) frameshift variant truncates the GluZincin functional domain (PVS1). The variant has not been reported in the gnomAD public database (PM2), and is located in a gene where LoF variation is constrained (pLI = 1.00) (ExAC). Biochemical/radiology results suggested a diagnosis of X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets (PP4). Together this indicates that the variant is predicted to be pathogenic.


This result CONFIRMS the clinical diagnosis of X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets in Patient.

FURTHER WORK
If appropriate, testing can be offered to patient?s parents. We recommend that they are referred to a local Clinical Genetics department to discuss this prior to testing.



NOTES
This case was not presented at WES MDT but discussed with referring clinician via email. Outcome of discussions are documented in Moka/Test notes
PHEX gene nomenclature based on GenBank accession numbers NM_000444.5 where nucleotide number 1 corresponds to the first base of the translation initiation codon
Method:
WES capture was performed using Agilent SureSelectXT Clinical Research Exome (SureSelectXT Human All Exon V5 baited with clinically relevant genes). The enriched exome libraries were sequenced using paired-end, 150 cycle chemistry on an Illumina NextSeq 550
Data Processing: 
Data processing by MokaWES v1.4 (demultiplexing bcl2fastq, alignment BWA-MEM, variant calling & coverage GATK)
Panel details: Genes tested within virtual panel and horizontal coverage
The list of genes tested and their horizontal coverage is attached. Horizontal coverage is determined using coding exons (+/- 5bp) to a minimum depth of 20X
Assessment of pathogenicity: 
Performed using QIAGEN Ingenuity Variant Analysis (CADD, CentoMD, EVS, Allele Frequency Community, JASPAR, Ingenuity Knowledge Base, Vista Enhancer, OMIM, gnomAD, Clinical Trials, BSIFT, TCGA, PolyPhen-2, 1000 Genome Frequency, Clinvar, DGV, COSMIC, ExAC, HGMD, PhyloP, DbSNP, TargetScan, SIFT4G), and Alamut for splice site analysis (SpliceSiteFinder-like, MaxEntScan, NNSplice, GeneSplicer)
Classifications are performed according to ACMG guidelines, ref: Richards et al, 2015 Genet Med. 17:405-424
Limitations of the assay
This WES analysis will not detect genomic rearrangements such as copy number variation, inversions and larger insertions/deletions. Intronic variants -/+5bp of the coding exons are not assessed.  
In addition, as some genes within our panels are known to have associated pseudo-genes, we cannot exclude the possibility of false negative results for these genes. 
The sensitivity and specificity of the WES analysis was determined to be
SNV: Sensitivity 99.20%: (95% CI: 99.20% to 99.30%), specificity 100%: (95% CI: 100% to 100%) 
SNV+InDel: Sensitivity 98.70%: (95% CI: 98.57 % to 98.82 %), specificity 100%: (95% CI: 100% to 100%) 
(This was performed using the GIAB sample, NA12878 and Agilent Exome v5, HiSeq2500 and PE100)
Clinical pick-up rate
WES has been reported to provide a molecular genetic diagnosis in ~30% of cases (Ann Neurol 2014; 76:473-483, N Engl J Med 2013; 369:1502-11, http://www.irdirc.org/wp-content/uploads/2014/11/T1S2-1_GilissenC.pdf, SciTM 2014; Vol 6 Issue 265 ra168)



cc:	Oxford Medical Genetics Laboratories 
Page 1 of 2
Please note: 1. Any DNA remaining after completion of the above tests is stored for potential use in the future.    2.  The above results and interpretations assume that (a) samples received by the laboratory are correctly identified, (b) family relationships given by consultants are true, and (c) the clinical diagnosis is as stated.   3. In order to avoid error and/or misinterpretation, transcription of all or part of this report is inadvisable.
